sampling_model.design: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent draws from the fully specified finite paired-cell law \(P_{m,h}\), and the label \(m\) is observed.
sampling_model.units: Each normalized unit has \(X=(m,V,J,Z)\), source \(S\), treatment \(T\), observed outcome \(Y=1/2+B\in\{1/2,3/2\}\), and potential outcomes supported on \([0,2]\).
sampling_model.treatment: Conditionally on \(X\), \(S\) and \(T\) are independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\); in the experimental source, treatment is randomized.
sampling_model.overlap: Every design, source, and treatment probability equals \(1/2\), and all Bernoulli outcome probabilities are uniformly inside \((0,1)\) for \(h\in H_m\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the \(2m\) informative gaps are unknown. They are estimated by capped informative-cell means with the explicit zero convention for empty cells. The proved mean-square and tail controls are derived from the fixed binomial experiment. With \(r^{\mathrm{cap}}_{n,m}=\min\{2a_m,\sqrt{32m\log(6m/\delta_0)/n}\}\), simultaneous truncated intervals centered at those capped means cover the entire coordinate vector with probability at least \(1-\delta_0\), including empty cells and cube boundaries. Their exact absolute-average images give the globally honest capped-cell endpoint rectangle and its \(\sqrt{m\log m/n}\)-type length bound. On fixed-dimensional separated profiles, the signed-cell rule remains only a uniformly asymptotically valid regular benchmark.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Lemma 1 and Theorem 1 derive sharp max/min sensitivity endpoints, while Section 5 replaces them by fixed-temperature Boltzmann approximations for influence-function inference.
The paper defines minimum expected length at a fixed function among globally honest intervals and attains its local-modulus benchmark for monotone and convex regression.
The paper proves the sharp minimax mean-squared-error frontier for an average absolute Gaussian mean by composite priors and Hermite-polynomial estimators.
The paper characterizes adaptive honest confidence intervals for linear functionals through between-class and ordered moduli.
The paper establishes lower bounds on pointwise expected interval length under uniform coverage and shows that honest adaptation can fail.
Section 5.4 gives a fixed-smoothing Wald interval and leaves data-driven tuning for the shortest confidence interval open.
Theorem 2 and Corollary D.1 establish asymptotic inference for deterministic entropic regularization under margin and nuisance-rate conditions.
The paper proves minimax point-estimation rates for nonsmooth discrete-distribution functionals using best-polynomial approximation and unbiased discrete moments.
The paper constructs one-at-a-time functional intervals by constrained likelihood-ratio inversion in linear Gaussian inverse problems.

body.tldr: Sharp data-fusion sensitivity endpoints are averages of absolute paired-cell gaps, so exact and near ties create a confidence problem that fixed smoothing does not resolve. The exact-tie and low-information frontiers are proved, and a capped-cell coordinate rectangle now gives a finite-sample globally honest endpoint pair with expected summed length of order \(k\min\{a_m,\sqrt{m\log(6m/\delta_0)/n}\}\). Combined with oracle positivity, it yields the global adaptation upper envelope \(C_0\min\{\max(1,a_m\sqrt n),\sqrt{m\log(6m/\delta_0)}\}\). No matching higher-information lower bound, globally optimal family, or resolution of the logarithmic factor is claimed. Causally, the experiment is a faithful finite paired-cell specialized subclass of the Lanners--Rudin--Volfovsky--Parikh sensitivity model, not the actual Project STAR sampling law or the unrestricted nonparametric model.

project_justification.gap: Published data-fusion work identifies the max/min endpoints and uses fixed smoothing, while existing confidence-adaptation and absolute-functional theories do not evaluate the full heterogeneous paired-binomial connected-interval oracle or its simultaneous adaptation cost. The capped-cell rectangle proves a global \(\sqrt{m\log m/n}\)-type honest upper envelope, but no matching higher-information lower bound establishes whether the \(\sqrt{m\log m}\) adaptation ceiling is sharp or whether the logarithm can be removed.
project_justification.niche: The fixed learnable experiment is a faithful finite paired-cell specialized subclass, or fiber, of the Lanners--Rudin--Volfovsky--Parikh model: treatment and study propensities are fixed at \(1/2\), the covariate law and outcome regressions are specialized, and \(\rho=\gamma=1/5\). This isolates tie uncertainty for both causal endpoints under joint coverage without claiming unrestricted nonparametric data-fusion inference.
project_justification.fill: The proved results combine paired-binomial testing with exact-tie and low-information lower bounds, a capped quadratic construction, a full-range low-information rule, and a capped-cell coordinate rectangle. The latter is uniformly finite-sample honest and has expected summed length at most \(C_0k\min\{a_m,\sqrt{m\log(6m/\delta_0)/n}\}\), yielding an explicit global adaptation upper envelope and an elbow at \(na_m^2/m\asymp\log m\). The higher-information profile, the matching adaptation lower bound, logarithmic necessity, one globally optimal family, and the Bernstein-degree certificate remain open.

body.related_work: ColnetMayerEtAl2024 surveys broader trial--observational fusion without a tie-adaptive endpoint-confidence result. LannersRudinVolfovskyParikh2025 supplies the general sensitivity-bound algebra and motivates the applied endpoint question; the present paired-cell law is a controlled specialized subclass with propensities fixed at \(1/2\), not an analysis of the actual Project STAR sampling law. CaiLowXia2013 supplies the closest local expected-length criterion, but its ordered shape-constrained Gaussian geometry does not cover this nonlinear absolute average. CaiLow2011 supplies composite-prior and polynomial tools for the absolute-value cusp, but only for minimax point estimation. CaiLow2004 and Low1997 organize honest adaptation for linear functionals and coverage-to-testing logic. LevisBonviniZengKeeleKennedy2025 leaves shortest-interval smoothing selection open, while BenMichael2025 handles deterministic growing regularization under margin conditions. JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015 motivates factorial moments for sparse cells, and BatllePatilStanleyOwhadiKuusela2024 motivates finite-sample test inversion in constrained linear Gaussian inverse problems.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact-tie oracle is characterized for every \(n,m\), and the full heterogeneous oracle and sharp adaptation factor are characterized only in the stated low-information regime. The capped-cell rectangle improves the former inverse-probability rectangle to expected summed length \(C_0k\min\{a_m,\sqrt{m\log(6m/\delta_0)/n}\}\) and yields a global adaptation upper envelope with ceiling \(\sqrt{m\log m}\), but it does not establish sharpness, logarithmic necessity, or a globally oracle-optimal family. Beyond the low-information regime, the mixed tie--boundary slice, connected-hull length after selection, and a sufficient Bernstein certificate degree remain unresolved.
body.honest_scope: The causal completion class \(\mathcal M_{m,h}\) is a faithful finite paired-cell specialized subclass, or fiber, of the Lanners--Rudin--Volfovsky--Parikh sensitivity model. Its treatment and study propensities are fixed at \(1/2\), its covariate distribution and outcome regressions are specialized, and \(\rho=\gamma=1/5\). Positivity, experimental internal validity, the relative-mean sensitivity restrictions, compatibility, and uniformly interior endpoint-attaining completions are verified. Raw expected-length lower bounds on this embedded experiment obstruct any procedure required to be honest over a supermodel containing it, but submodel oracle upper bounds and adaptation-factor rates do not automatically transfer to the unrestricted published class. The capped-cell rectangle is finite-sample jointly honest on the displayed experiment and yields a global upper envelope; it is not asserted to be globally oracle-optimal. The construction reproduces the same sensitivity-bound algebra used in the Project STAR analysis in a controlled subexperiment, but it does not analyze the actual Project STAR sampling law.
